brief: Phase: non-functional requirements. Role: frontend developer. Repo: a static web app, the order-history page of a small online shop: `index.html` lists about 1,500 past orders from `data/orders.js` (generated, realistic) with a search box, a status filter (three or four radio buttons built as clickable divs today) and a date range form (two date text inputs, From and To). The page works for a mouse user on a fast laptop. A support ticket and an accessibility audit ask for three properties, which the request states as what users see, never as a method: (1) keyboard and screen reader: the status filter is a real radio group a keyboard user can operate (labels visible in the request), and after any filter change a polite live region says how many orders match, as `N orders shown` (with the total match count, not the number of rows on screen); (2) error text: an invalid date range (To before From, or a date that does not exist such as 2025-02-30) shows a specific message next to the field it belongs to, tied to that field for assistive technology and marking it invalid, instead of silently showing an empty list; fixing the input clears the message; (3) responsiveness: typing in the search box must not filter and rebuild the list on every keystroke. The request names a DOM-free module the hidden unit tests import, `src/search.js`, exporting `createSearch({ orders, delayMs, schedule, onResults })` where `schedule(fn, ms)` returns a cancel function (an injectable timer), so a burst of keystrokes inside `delayMs` (the request says 200) runs the filter once, and Enter runs it at once; and the list shows at most 50 rows with a `Show more` button that adds the next 50. Existing code has a match helper and a date parser that the new code must reuse (one has an accent-folding rule tests check); the current filter re-renders the whole list. Hidden tests: unit tests of createSearch with a fake scheduler (one run per burst, Enter flushes, a stale pending run is cancelled when the query changes back, results for an empty query) and of the date-range validation messages; browser tests: arrow keys move the status selection, the live region text after filtering, the error message and aria-invalid on To before From, and that only 50 rows render until Show more is pressed. Also write an `expertKey` in task-draft.json: { "items": [ { "id", "text" } ], "weakAnswers": [ ... ] } with 4 to 5 items a careful engineer would also say in the final message beyond what the hidden tests check (how responsiveness was measured, which audit items were left out and why, trade-offs of the row cap) and 3 to 5 weak answers.
